verdict.line: You win if you force fights the instant his Q (Rupture) goes on cooldown and you're past level 3; you lose if you walk up on an up Rupture and eat repeated 950-range pokes before you're ever close enough to use your own kit.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath's Q (Rupture) reaches 950 range while your longest tool, E (Slice and Dice), only reaches 450 — this lane is a fight over that 500-unit gap, not a fight about who's stronger once engaged. Once you're actually on him, your stun chain and healing Q win the trade clean, which is why the data hands Renekton the lane-state and solo-kill edge. The 42.2% win rate over 187 games exists because closing that gap safely, over and over, is harder than winning the fight once you get there.

theirWindow.what: He can drop Rupture on your approach path from 950 range to pop you airborne and slow you before you're anywhere near E range, then walk or auto freely while you're still closing — don't cross open ground into an up Rupture.

yourWindow.when: the instant he throws Rupture, hit or miss
yourWindow.what: Rupture is on a 9s cooldown, so the moment it's cast he has no way to zone you for a full 9 seconds — dash in immediately with E (Slice and Dice, 450 range) and chain into W (Ruthless Predator) before he can reset distance.

start.why: 45.9% win rate over 37 games — the regen and reduced poke damage directly offset a lane built around Cho chipping you down with 950-range Q pokes rather than all-inning you early.

boots.why: 71.3% pick, 43.8% win rate — the tenacity shortens how long Feral Scream's silence locks you out of your stun chain, and the magic resist eats into his Q/W/R magic damage.

core.why: Its proc shield absorbs part of a Rupture or Feral Scream hit right as you commit to the all-in, and the burst punishes the exact engage-then-double-hit pattern your empowered W and E already create.

Cho permanently gains max HP every time Feast kills something (up to 6 stacks), so the stacking armor shred — on top of E's own empowered armor reduction — is what keeps your damage from bouncing off him late.

he's stacked up toward 6 Feast kills and is sitting on a much larger HP bar than you

runes.keystoneWhy: This lane is a grind over who controls the gap, not a single burst window — Conqueror's stacking adaptive force and healing build up across the repeated Q trades and E dash-ins this matchup forces, then pay off as sustain once you're finally fighting at range zero.

summoners.why: 83.6% pick rate — Ignite seals the kills your solo-kill edge is supposed to convert once you close the gap and land a stun chain. Flash+Teleport (15% pick) is the alternative if you're playing this lane for scaling and side-wave pressure instead of forcing early kills.

playing.title: Bank Fury before engaging
playing.detail: Only all-in once Fury sits above 50 — it turns W (Ruthless Predator) from a 2-hit 0.75s stun into a 3-hit 1.5s stun that strips any shield, and boosts Q's damage and heal.

playing.title: Engage in the 9s dead zone
playing.detail: The instant Rupture is thrown, hit or miss, he has no ranged poke for 9 full seconds — dash in with E during that window instead of walking into a loaded Q.

playing.title: Don't commit into an up Feral Scream
playing.detail: Feral Scream silences and can shut down your W/E chain mid-combo; bait it on cooldown (13s) with a short poke rather than starting your full stun sequence into it.

playing.title: Track Feast once he's stacking
playing.detail: Feast is a 60s-cooldown true-damage execute at 175 range that permanently grows him on a kill — don't all-in at HP where one Feast finishes you, and look to fight right after he's used it.

playing.title: Shred his stacking HP with Cleaver
playing.detail: Every Feast kill makes him permanently tankier, so your armor shred from Cleaver and empowered E is what keeps your damage relevant into the mid-late game.

playing.title: Force fights at 3 and 6, not later
playing.detail: The data gives you lane and solo-kill advantage early; the longer the lane goes even, the more his poke and stacking close that gap, so use the level 3 stun and level 6 ultimate to fight on your terms.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and timing advice are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of being hit with Cho’Gath’s (Q). Slowly build up Fury and wait for an opportunity to close in on him to gain lane control.
